identity.title: LoRA Training Provably Converges to a Low-Rank Global Minimum Or It Fails Loudly (But it Probably Won't Fail)

problem.claim: Analyze LoRA’s loss landscape and training dynamics without restrictive linearization assumptions.

gap.claim: Prior LoRA analyses relied on linearization arguments or highly simplified setups, leaving theoretical understanding limited.

contributions.claim: Defines special and generic regimes to distinguish idealized settings where linearization applies from more realistic settings where it does not.
In the generic regime, characterizes training as converging either to a low-rank, small-magnitude global minimizer or to a qualitatively distinct high-rank, large-magnitude solution.
Argues that zero initialization and weight decay bias LoRA toward the low-rank, small-magnitude region containing global minima.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present an analysis of the LoRA loss landscape without the restrictive assumptions used in prior analyses.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report the generic-regime dichotomy between convergence to a low-rank, small-magnitude global minimizer and convergence to a high-rank, large-magnitude solution.
The authors argue that LoRA’s zero initialization and weight decay create an implicit bias toward the region where global minima lie.

narrative_sequence.summary: LoRA is presented as a standard method for fine-tuning foundation models.
Existing theoretical analyses are described as limited by linearization or highly simplified setups.
The paper introduces special and generic regimes, separating idealized linearizable cases from more realistic non-linearizable cases.
For the generic regime, the authors report a low-rank global-minimum versus high-rank large-magnitude outcome dichotomy.
The authors attribute LoRA’s usual success to an implicit bias from zero initialization and weight decay.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates idealized and realistic settings before stating a regime-specific convergence result.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the scope and conditions of a theoretical claim easier to identify.
lessons.application: Define explicit operating regimes before presenting guarantees or convergence conclusions.
lessons.exception: Avoid regime splitting when the distinctions are not mathematically or practically meaningful.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, optimization algorithm, convergence conditions, or formal meaning of rank and magnitude in the reported dichotomy.
It does not provide empirical measurements establishing how often the proposed failure outcome occurs or how often LoRA finds global minima.
